AfterCombatVictory.issue: Rollup of guard G1 per binding rule 4. The heal itself is faithful (6 HP, `!IsDead`, no ascension branch); what diverges is the hook the sim maps it onto -- one collapsed on_combat_end(player_won) instead of C#'s separate AfterCombatEnd/AfterCombatVictory pair, with no ReviveBeforeCombatEnd step in between.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): AfterCombatVictory and AfterCombatEnd are one sim hook, and the sim has no ReviveBeforeCombatEnd
guards.issue: MECHANISM: C# reaches AfterCombatEnd and AfterCombatVictory only through EndCombatInternal (CombatManager.cs:970-999), which is the VICTORY path; a loss goes LoseCombat -> _pendingLoss -> ProcessPendingLoss (CombatManager.cs:945-965, 1046-1052) and fires NO hook at all. EndCombatInternal also runs `await player.ReviveBeforeCombatEnd()` (Player.cs:821-827, heal-to-1) before either hook. The sim collapses both hooks into one `on_combat_end(player_won)` (combat.py:347-350) and has no revive step. audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json step 71 / guard G10 already verdicts this mechanism a gap and labels it DORMANT, and names this exact relic file as one of the four ported on_combat_end listeners it read to establish the dormancy. One verdict per mechanism (binding rule 3): this record cites it and does not re-derive it. Rule 7: CombatManager.cs, Player.cs and sts2_rl/combat.py are NOT hashed by this record. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT LIVE for this relic: an AfterCombatVictory-only listener whose effect is unconditional (this one is not -- it gates on player_won), or a sim path that reaches on_combat_end(player_won=True) with a dead player that C# would have revived. Both codebases currently agree on every reachable outcome, which is what makes it dormant rather than live.

guards.rationale: The two guards have opposite standing and the same result. C#'s is effectively dead code in single-player: ReviveBeforeCombatEnd has already healed a dead player to 1 HP by the time AfterCombatVictory runs, so IsDead is false -- the guard exists for a downed co-op player. The sim's IS live, because there is no revive; but the only sim path that can declare a win with a dead player is combat.py:302-305 (all enemies die to an on_enemy_turn_start effect that also kills the player), and C# resolves exactly that race as a LOSS -- CheckWinCondition tests _pendingLoss before IsEnding (CombatManager.cs:1046-1057) -- where it likewise heals nothing. Same observable on every reachable path. Rule 7: neither CombatManager.cs nor combat.py is hashed here.
